name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Unpaid Salary and Withholding Relieving Letter after Resignation
case_dossier.summary: The employee resigned after completing a 60‑day notice, handed over all assets and received a clearance certificate, but the September salary plus encashable leave (Rs 1,65,000) remains unpaid and the employer is refusing to issue the relieving and experience letters, jeopardising the new job offer.
case_dossier.opposite_party: IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram (Employer)

timeline.event: Completed handover of assets (MacBook, ID card) and received asset clearance certificate

timeline.date_or_period: By 19 Nov 2024 (≈50 days after last working day)
timeline.event: September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (Rs 1,65,000) still unpaid
HR replies that finance team faces client payment delays; relieving and experience letters are being withheld
New employer threatens to cancel job offer unless relieving letter is provided

evidence_held: Email correspondence with HR indicating salary delay and withholding of relieving letter
evidence_needed: Salary slips for August and September 2024
Bank statements or UPI transaction records showing non‑receipt of September salary
Copy of employment contract showing salary and notice period terms
Written request (email/WhatsApp) sent to employer demanding pending salary and relieving letter
Any written communication from employer stating reason for withholding relieving letter
Proof of new employer's requirement (e.g., email requesting relieving letter)
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Existing documents confirm resignation and asset clearance, but lack concrete proof of unpaid salary and the employer's refusal, lowering the overall strength.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a clear legal right to receive the salary you earned up to your last working day and to get the relieving/experience letters you need for your new job. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employer must pay all wages due within two working days after an employee resigns (Section 17(2)). The fact that you handed over all company property, completed the notice period and have a clearance certificate shows you fulfilled your side of the contract. The employer’s refusal to pay your September salary and to give the relieving letter is a breach of that contract and a civil matter, not a criminal offence. You can therefore claim the unpaid amount and ask the court or labour authority to order the employer to issue the required documents.

governing_laws.relevance: Requires the employer to pay all wages within two working days of resignation, dismissal or retrenchment.
Limits any deductions to a maximum of 50% of wages; ensures the employer cannot withhold salary by claiming excessive deductions.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Shows that non‑payment of salary and refusal to issue relieving letters are civil disputes, not criminal cheating.

action_options.title: Send a Formal Legal Notice (Demand Letter)
action_options.timeline: Within 7 days of sending the notice
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (postage/WhatsApp/Email). You can draft it yourself using a template.
action_options.details: Write a clear, polite but firm email (or registered post) addressed to the HR/Finance head. Cite Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages and request: (a) payment of Rs 1,65,000 within 2 working days of receipt of this notice, and (b) issuance of the relieving and experience letters within 5 days. Attach copies of your resignation acceptance, asset clearance certificate, and any prior salary‑delay emails. Keep a copy for your records.

action_options.title: File a Complaint on the Labour Department’s e‑Daakhil / DOL Portal
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs; only nominal filing charges if any.
action_options.details: Register on the Ministry of Labour’s e‑Daakhil portal (https://edakhil.gov.in). Choose ‘Recovery of Wages’ under the Code on Wages. Upload the legal notice, resignation acceptance, asset clearance, salary slips (if available) and bank statements showing non‑receipt. The Labour Commissioner will issue a notice to the employer and may order payment within a set period. Follow up through the portal’s tracking feature.

action_options.title: Approach the Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal (or Civil Court) for Recovery and Injunctive Relief
action_options.timeline: 60‑90 days after filing the labour‑department complaint, if the employer still does not comply
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal court fees (around Rs 500‑1,000 for a claim of Rs 1.65 Lakhs). You may also claim legal costs later.
action_options.details: Prepare a plaint stating breach of employment contract and non‑payment of wages under Section 17(2). Attach all evidence: resignation email, clearance certificate, copy of the legal notice, employer’s response (if any), and proof of the new employer’s requirement. You can represent yourself in the Labour Court; however, if the employer contests, consider engaging a lawyer for drafting and representation. The court can order: (a) payment of the pending salary with interest, (b) issuance of relieving/experience letters, and (c) compensation for any loss caused by the delay.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can start with steps 1 and 2 on your own – drafting a notice and filing on the e‑Daakhil portal do not require a lawyer. If the employer contests the claim, ignores the labour‑department notice, or you need to claim additional damages, a qualified labour‑law advocate will help you draft the plaint, represent you in the Labour Court, and ensure procedural compliance. The Consumer Forum does not have jurisdiction over employment matters, so a labour‑law specialist is the right choice.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**[Your Letterhead – if any]** --- ## LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE *(Under the Code on Wages, 2019 – Sections 17(2) & 18(3))* --- ### 1. Date & Mode of Dispatch | Date (dd‑mm‑yyyy) | Mode of Dispatch | |-------------------|------------------| | **07‑Nov‑2024** | **Speed Post (Acknowledgement Due)** *(or Registered Email with read‑receipt)* | --- ### 2. Parties | **From (Sender – Complainant)** | **To (Recipient – Employer)** | |--------------------------------|--------------------------------| | **Name:** ______________________
**Designation (at time of employment):** Front‑End Developer
**Address:** ______________________
**Phone / Email:** ______________________ | **Name of Firm:** ______________________ (IT‑Consultancy Firm)
**Registered Office:** ______________________, Cyber City, Gurugram, Haryana – 122002
**Attention:** HR / Finance Head – ______________________
**Phone / Email:** ______________________ | --- ### 3. Under Instructions From My Client The undersigned, **[Your Name]**, acting on his/her own behalf, hereby submits the following facts and demands: --- ### 4. Factual Matrix | Date / Period | Event | |---------------|-------| | **01‑Aug‑2024** | Submitted resignation email to the Employer, tendering a 60‑day notice. | | **01‑Aug – 30‑Sep‑2024** | Served full notice period; performed duties diligently. | | **30‑Sep‑2024** | Completed hand‑over of all company assets (MacBook, ID‑card, etc.) and obtained a **Asset Clearance Certificate** signed by the Employer. | | **Early‑Sep‑2024** | August salary was **delayed** (paid after the statutory period). | | **By 19‑Nov‑2024** (≈ 50 days after last working day) | September salary **plus 15 days encashable leave** (total **Rs 1,65,000**) remains **unpaid**. | | **Ongoing since salary delay** | HR communicated that the Finance team is awaiting client payments and consequently **withholds the relieving & experience letters**. | | **Mid‑Nov‑2024 (end of week)** | New employer has **threatened to cancel the job offer** unless the relieving letter is produced. | **Documents in possession (Annexure‑A):** 1. Appointment Letter. 2. Resignation acceptance email (dated 01‑Aug‑2024). 3. Signed Asset Clearance Certificate (dated 30‑Sep‑2024). 4. Email thread with HR regarding salary delay & withholding of relieving letter. **Documents to be produced by the Employer (Annexure‑B, if any):** - Salary slips for August & September 2024. - Bank/UPI statements evidencing non‑receipt of September salary. - Copy of the employment contract (showing salary & notice‑period terms). - Any written communication stating the reason for withholding the relieving letter. - Email/WhatsApp from the new employer requesting the relieving letter. --- ### 5. Legal Grounds 1. **Section 17(2), Code on Wages, 2019** – An employer **must pay all wages due** to an employee **within two working days** of the employee’s resignation, termination or retrenchment. 2. **Section 18(3), Code on Wages, 2019** – Deductions from wages cannot exceed **50 %** of the wages; withholding the entire salary is unlawful. 3. **General Contract Law (Indian Contract Act, 1872)** – The employee has fully performed his contractual obligations (notice served, assets returned, clearance obtained). The employer’s refusal to pay wages and to issue the relieving/experience letters constitutes a **breach of contract** and a **civil wrong**. 4. **Interest** – Under Section 35 of the Code on Wages, any amount due as wages shall attract **interest at the rate of 12 % per annum** from the date of default until actual payment. --- ### 6. Demand (Strict 15‑Day Rectification Window) > **You are hereby required to comply with the following, within **fifteen (15) calendar days** from the receipt of this notice (i.e., by **22‑Nov‑2024**):** 1. **Payment of the pending salary and encashable leave amounting to Rs 1,65,000 (Rupees One Lakh Sixty‑Five Thousand only)**, together with statutory interest at **12 % per annum** calculated from **20‑Oct‑2024** (the date the September salary became due) up to the date of actual payment. 2. **Issuance of the following documents, duly signed on the company’s letterhead, within five (5) days of the above payment:** - Relieving Letter confirming resignation acceptance and date of last working day. - Experience/Service Certificate reflecting the period of employment and designation. 3. **Confirmation in writing (email or registered post) that the above obligations have been fulfilled**, addressed to the undersigned at the address mentioned above. --- ### 7. Consequence of Non‑Compliance If any of the above demands are **not fully satisfied within the stipulated 15‑day period**, the undersigned **shall be constrained to initiate legal proceedings** without further notice, which may include but are not limited to: 1. **Filing a complaint before the Labour Commissioner (e‑Daakhil / DOL portal) for recovery of wages** under the Code on Wages, 2019, seeking a **mandamus order** for payment of the dues with interest and costs. 2. **Instituting suit before the appropriate Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal** for: - Recovery of the unpaid salary and leave encashment with statutory interest (12 % p.a.). - Specific performance – i.e., compulsory issuance of the relieving and experience letters. - Compensation for loss suffered due to the new employer’s threatened withdrawal of the job offer (damages as may be quantified). - Recovery of **legal costs, court fees, and any other expenses** incurred. **Please note:** The statutory interest will continue to accrue until the date of actual payment, and the employer will be liable for **legal costs** as per the provisions of the Code on Wages and the Civil Procedure Code, 1908. --- ### 8. Annexures | Annexure | Description | |----------|-------------| | **Annexure‑A** | Copy of Appointment Letter, Resignation Acceptance Email, Asset Clearance Certificate, HR email correspondence (salary delay & withholding). | | **Annexure‑B** | (To be produced by Employer) Salary slips for Aug‑2024 & Sep‑2024; Bank/UPI statements showing non‑receipt; Employment contract copy; Any written justification for withholding relieving letter; New employer’s email requesting relieving letter. | | **Annexure‑C** | Draft of this Legal Demand Notice (for reference). | --- ### 9. sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, aapki resignation aur clearance certificate humare records mein aagayi hai, lekin finance department ko abhi bhi aapke asset handover ki final verification karni hai. Company policy ke mutabik salary aur relieving letter ka processing minimum 7 din ka hota hai, aur humare paas abhi kuch pending approvals hain. Isliye aapko thoda aur samay dena padega – hum aapka case agle 5 din mein dekh lenge. Agar aap turant payment chahte hain, to aapko apni resignation ki original copy aur asset handover receipt dobara bhejna hoga, tabhi hum aage badh sakte hain.
